Open • FLYBYME (Tim) opened about 1 minute ago • 0 comments


   releaseCrud  ( mesh-serve/src/cdn/contracts/release.contract.ts ) declares:
                                                                              
    visibility: { find: 'public', findOne: 'public', get: 'public', count:    
  'public' }                                                                  
                                                                              
  and its own comment, at line 40, explains why that is safe:                 
                                                                              
  │ It is exposable now because  scopedBy  makes every generated read a read  
  │ within the caller's                                                       
  │ own organization — the mechanism, not the discipline, is what makes this  
  │ line safe to write.                                                       
                                                                              
   releaseCrud  declares no  scopedBy . There is no default:                  
  normalizeUniqueKeys  in the                                                 
  framework says "On an unscoped collection: all keys are global". So         
  release.find  answers with                                                  
  every composition on the platform — which parts each tenant runs, at which  
  versions, at which                                                          
  digests — to anyone who can reach a site that exposes it.                   
                                                                              
   siteCrud  next door does declare  scopedBy: 'tenantId'  (line 81), which is
  why this reads as                                                           
  done when you skim it. The comment is not wrong about the rule; it states   
  the condition that would                                                    
  make the exposure safe, in the same object that fails to meet it.           
                                                                              
  ## What to do                                                               
                                                                              
  1. Add  scopedBy: 'tenantId'  to  releaseCrud , and check what it breaks —  
  unique: [{ fields:                                                          
  'hash', scope: 'global' }]  is deliberate and must stay global (two people  
  composing the same                                                          
  set have composed the same release), so confirm the framework still accepts 
  a global unique key                                                         
  on a scoped collection. If it does not, say so in a comment before working  
  around it.                                                                  
  2. Audit every  defineCrud  in the repository and record the decision on    
  each, in its own doc                                                        
  comment: scoped, or global-on-purpose-and-here-is-why. Current state:       
    •  site  — scoped ✅                                                      
    •  release  — this issue                                                  
    •  artifact ,  part ,  partVersion  — global on purpose, each says why.   
    Leave them.                                                               
    •  build  — unscoped, and nobody decided that. A build row names a        
    repository and a commit.                                                  
    It is not currently exposed, so this is a decision to make rather than a  
    hole to close.                                                            
    •  node ,  group  — a fleet belongs to the deployment rather than to an   
    organization. Probably                                                    
    right; make it explicit either way.                                       
  3.  test/api/visibility.test.ts  already has a test for this, marked  it.   
  fails . Delete the                                                          
   .fails  when you fix it — that marker exists so the suite goes red the     
  moment this works,                                                          
  and a fix that leaves it is a fix nobody can see.                           
                                                                              
  ## Watch out                                                                
                                                                              
   cdn.compose  and the rolling-release handler ( src/cdn/methods/rolling.ts )
  both read and write                                                         
  releases, and the rolling handler runs from an event with no caller — it    
  passes a constructed meta                                                   
  for the release's own tenant. Scoping the collection will affect it. There  
  are tests                                                                   
  ( test/cdn/rolling.test.ts ).                                               
                                                                              
  Related: the same class of problem, one level down, is that  visibility  is 
  not enforced at                                                             
  dispatch at all — only in  describeExposure . That is a separate issue and  
  not yours; do not                                                           
  try to fix it here.                                                         


View this issue on GitHub: https://github.com/FLYBYME/surfdns/issues/60
